To swap the video, drop the new file in, point `video` at it and rewrite the lines and times here; nothing else needs to change. Delete this file and the page falls back to the narration drafted during the walkthrough. Times measured from the clip's own narration audio by tools/time_final_video_captions.py - re-run it after re-rendering the video, or every line drifts.

captions.text: The framework processes an input image using a hybrid architecture designed to build a powerful global representation for image retrieval.
First, a convolutional neural network stem maps the raw input image to a feature tensor, introducing inductive bias in the early layers.
A dynamic position embedding module then dynamically resamples fixed-size learned embeddings to match the size of each mini-batch.
The sequence is then fed into a Vision Transformer encoder consisting of multiple layers.
The input sequence consists of a classification token and patch token embeddings.
The sequence passes through the first transformer encoding layer.
This layer outputs updated classification and patch token embeddings.
The tokens continue to propagate through successive intermediate layers of the encoder.
Finally, they reach the deeper layers of the transformer encoder.
The final layers produce the final set of classification and patch token embeddings.
To capture multi-layer classification features, the classification tokens from several of the last layers are collected and concatenated.
These concatenated classification tokens form the input to the global branch.
A fully connected layer projects these multi-layer classification features into a lower-dimensional space.
This yields the final global feature representation.
Simultaneously, the local branch collects multi-layer patch features, unfolding them into three-dimensional tensors to preserve spatial information.
These unfolded patch features from multiple layers are then concatenated.
This forms a multi-layer spatial tensor representation.
A one-by-one convolution is applied to reduce the channel dimension of the concatenated features.
The reduced features are processed by an enhanced locality module to strengthen local interactions in the deeper layers.
The enhanced features are then fused with the original reduced features.
Global average pooling and a fully connected layer are applied to produce the final local feature.
The global feature and local feature are concatenated to combine global and local information.
This forms a unified representation of the image.
A final fully connected layer with dropout and batch normalization reduces the dimensionality.
The resulting representation is optimized using the ArcFace loss function during the training phase.
